comments.note: Application\AI\Cache\Strategies\FixedDurationStrategy still uses the implicit filemtime()-false arithmetic pattern (time() - filemtime(...) < $duration). R2 only required the guard on the API version, so this is in-scope. However, the same risky pattern exists here: if filemtime() returns false, PHP coerces it to 0 and the TTL check incorrectly evaluates the file as expired (treating age as time()). Flag for a follow-up quality pass to apply the same guard consistently.

No test coverage for STRATEGY_ID constant values or getID() return values in the strategy unit tests. Given the AC is purely structural (constants and docblocks), code inspection is sufficient, but a 2-line assertion per strategy would prevent silent regressions.

comments.note: AI\Cache\Strategies\FixedDurationStrategy::isCacheFileValid() still uses implicit filemtime() arithmetic: (time() - filemtime($cacheFile->getPath()) < $durationInSeconds). If filemtime() returns false, PHP coerces false to 0 making the subtraction ~1.7 billion — the file is treated as expired, which is safe, but the behaviour relies on type coercion rather than an explicit guard. The API counterpart (fixed in R2) now has the explicit guard; consistency and PHPStan strict-mode correctness argue for applying the same fix here. Low-blocking today, but a follow-up WP should add the explicit guard for symmetry.

AI\Cache\Strategies\FixedDurationStrategy and UncachedStrategy lack @package/@subpackage class-level PHPDoc.
